limitations: Category grouping uses callFrame URL and self samples; compiled application URLs include bundled Next/dependency/shared modules and must not be treated as pure business logic.
Percentages use sampled thread elapsed intervals, including idle, GC, preemption and profiler overhead; they are not percentages of total process CPU and are not projected throughput gains.
Node built-in category includes node:inspector post: 200.55 sampled milliseconds, 1.22 percent.

Process counters include CPU profiler start/stop and profile-file processing around the phase; the nearly two-core sum is consistent with little quota headroom but no cgroup throttling delta was captured.
Inspector excludes native Prisma worker threads, MongoDB and load generator CPU.
Serial database probes expose millisecond-rounded indexed operations on one fixture; counts and server milliseconds do not measure contention or whole-ramp query attribution.
Cold serial create includes first AccountingPeriod creation; its 28 operations are not a guaranteed count for every steady-state create.

A native-driver migration might remove some client conversion overhead but must be benchmarked with identical authorization, BSON/null semantics, transaction, number claim, print snapshot and audit behavior; no migration benefit is proven.
